question: Do fixed topic keywords in exported event summaries improve the same numeric baseline?
dataset_and_target: Same 66 TimesX KRW samples, 47 expanding-origin evaluations and 12-business-day mean-return target as pilot_protocol.json
primary_arm: K1 = B1 numeric/calendar/covariates + event count + eight topic mention rates per 1000 English words
controls: KS numeric plus preceding-origin keyword rates and event count
training: Same fixed ridge lambda=1, training-only scaling, no tuning; training target ends strictly before origin
features: Manually fixed English topic dictionaries matching the English benchmark, not learned from target outcomes. Case-insensitive token boundaries; longest multiword synonyms consumed once within each topic; rates normalized by word count.
primary_metric: Paired MAE difference B1 minus K1, all 47 origins and every calendar block
uncertainty: Same 5000-draw block bootstrap length 3, seed 20261026; descriptive only; multiple strategies have now been inspected on these outcomes
limitations: Original publication timestamps and source snapshots missing
Keyword frequency does not encode negation, direction, expectations, actor or causal effect
No full-context language model has been evaluated
No current probability or Seoul SME validity claim
